survivors.q: What is the name of Valencia's home stadium?
survivors.hint: Valencia have played at Mestalla since 1923, named after the irrigation channel that ran beside the site.

survivors.q: By what nickname are Valencia CF commonly known?
survivors.hint: "Che" is a Valencian interjection, and the club and its fans have long been known as Los Che.

survivors.q: Which animal appears on Valencia CF's club crest?
survivors.hint: The bat sits atop Valencia's crest, taken from the coat of arms of the city of Valencia.

survivors.q: Valencia lost the 2000 Champions League final to which club?
survivors.hint: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 in Paris in the first all-Spanish European Cup final.

survivors.q: Valencia lost the 2001 Champions League final to which club?
survivors.hint: Bayern Munich beat Valencia on penalties after a 1-1 draw, a second final defeat in a row for the Spanish side.

survivors.q: Which striker did Valencia sign from Real Zaragoza in 2005, going on to score more than 100 goals for the club?
survivors.hint: David Villa scored around 129 goals in five seasons at Valencia after arriving from Zaragoza in 2005.

survivors.q: Which club did David Silva join when he left Valencia in 2010?
survivors.hint: Silva moved from Valencia to Manchester City in the summer of 2010 and spent a decade there.

survivors.q: Who was Valencia's manager when they won the 2004 UEFA Cup?
survivors.hint: Rafael Benítez won both La Liga and the UEFA Cup with Valencia in 2003-04 before leaving for Liverpool.

survivors.q: In which decade was Valencia CF founded?
survivors.hint: Valencia CF was founded in March 1919, and marked their centenary during the 2018-19 season.

survivors.q: Which club are Valencia's city rivals in the Valencian derby?
survivors.hint: Levante UD are the other major club in the city of Valencia, making theirs the true city derby.

survivors.q: Which club did Valencia beat in the 2004 UEFA Cup final?
survivors.hint: Valencia beat Marseille 2-0 in the final in Gothenburg to complete a league-and-UEFA-Cup double.

survivors.q: Which club did Gaizka Mendieta join when he left Valencia in 2001?
survivors.hint: Mendieta left Valencia for Lazio in 2001 in one of the biggest transfers of the era.

survivors.q: Which manager led Valencia to both the 2000 and 2001 Champions League finals?
survivors.hint: Argentine coach Héctor Cúper took Valencia to back-to-back European Cup finals before joining Inter.

survivors.q: Which goalkeeper joined Valencia from Real Madrid in 1998 and went on to spend a decade at the club?
survivors.hint: Santiago Cañizares left Real Madrid for Valencia in 1998 and stayed until 2008, playing through the Cúper and Benítez trophy years.

survivors.q: At which stadium was the 2001 Champions League final, in which Valencia were beaten, played?
survivors.hint: The 2001 final between Bayern Munich and Valencia was staged at the San Siro in Milan.

survivors.q: Which Argentine centre-back joined Valencia in 2000 and became a mainstay of their title-winning defence?
survivors.hint: Roberto Ayala arrived from Milan in 2000 and anchored Valencia's defence through both La Liga titles.

survivors.q: Which club did Valencia beat in the 2019 Copa del Rey final?
survivors.hint: Valencia beat Barcelona 2-1 in Seville to win the Copa del Rey in their centenary season.

survivors.q: Valencia won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup in which two consecutive years?
survivors.hint: Valencia won the Fairs Cup in 1962 and retained it in 1963, then lost the 1964 final.

survivors.q: Which midfielder formed Valencia's central-midfield partnership with David Albelda under Rafael Benítez?
survivors.hint: Rubén Baraja and David Albelda were the double pivot behind Valencia's 2002 and 2004 league titles.

survivors.q: Which Norwegian striker did Valencia sign from Rosenborg in 2000?
survivors.hint: John Carew joined Valencia from Rosenborg in 2000 and played in the 2001 Champions League final.

survivors.q: How many consecutive La Liga seasons did Valencia finish third under Unai Emery?
survivors.hint: Emery's Valencia finished third in 2009-10, 2010-11 and 2011-12, behind Barcelona and Real Madrid each time.

survivors.q: Which English club did Valencia knock out in the semi-finals of the 2000-01 Champions League?
survivors.hint: Valencia drew 0-0 at Elland Road and won the second leg 3-0 at Mestalla to knock Leeds United out and reach the 2001 final.

survivors.q: Who managed Valencia to the 2008 Copa del Rey title?
survivors.hint: Ronald Koeman won the 2008 Copa del Rey against Getafe, then was sacked just days later with the club close to the relegation zone.

survivors.q: How many La Liga titles have Valencia won?
survivors.hint: Valencia's six league titles came in 1942, 1944, 1947, 1971, 2002 and 2004.

survivors.q: Which club did Valencia beat in the 1980 European Cup Winners' Cup final?
survivors.hint: Valencia beat Arsenal in the 1980 final in Brussels after a goalless 120 minutes.

survivors.q: Which businessman acquired a controlling stake in Valencia in 2014?
survivors.hint: Singaporean businessman Peter Lim took control of Valencia through Meriton Holdings in 2014.

survivors.q: Which Valencia player saw his penalty saved to end the 2001 Champions League final shootout?
survivors.hint: Mauricio Pellegrino's spot-kick was saved to hand Bayern Munich the trophy in Milan.

survivors.q: Which goalkeeper saved three Valencia penalties in the 2001 Champions League final shootout?
survivors.hint: Bayern's Oliver Kahn produced three saves in the shootout to win the 2001 final.

survivors.q: Valencia signed playmaker Pablo Aimar in 2001 from which Argentine club?
survivors.hint: Aimar joined Valencia from River Plate in January 2001 and stayed until 2006.

survivors.q: Who holds Valencia's record for most appearances for the club?
survivors.hint: Midfielder Fernando Gómez made over 550 appearances for Valencia between 1983 and 1998, a club record.

survivors.q: Which former Real Madrid great managed Valencia to the 1970-71 La Liga title?
survivors.hint: Alfredo Di Stéfano took charge at Mestalla in 1970 and won the league in his first season.

survivors.q: Valencia beat Real Madrid 2-0 in the 1979 Copa del Rey final — who scored both of their goals?
survivors.hint: Mario Kempes scored twice against Real Madrid to win Valencia the 1979 Copa del Rey.

survivors.q: Who was Valencia's manager when they beat Porto to win the 2004 UEFA Super Cup?
survivors.hint: Claudio Ranieri had returned for a second spell after Benítez left for Liverpool, and won the Super Cup in Monaco.

survivors.q: Which club did Valencia eliminate in the semi-finals of the 2003-04 UEFA Cup?
survivors.hint: Valencia beat regional rivals Villarreal in the semi-finals before defeating Marseille in the final.

survivors.q: Valencia's opening goal in the 2004 UEFA Cup final was a penalty converted by which player?
survivors.hint: Winger Vicente Rodríguez scored from the spot before Mista added the second in the 2-0 win over Marseille.

survivors.q: Bayer Leverkusen play their home matches at which stadium?
survivors.hint: Leverkusen's ground on Bismarckstraße has carried the BayArena name since 1998; the other three are the homes of Dortmund, Bayern Munich and Schalke.

survivors.q: By which nickname is Bayer Leverkusen commonly known?
survivors.hint: "Die Werkself" means "the works eleven": the club was founded in 1904 by employees of the Bayer chemical plant. Die Fohlen, Die Knappen and Die Roten Bullen belong to Mönchengladbach, Schalke and RB Leipzig.

survivors.q: Leverkusen reached the 2002 Champions League final. Which club beat them?
survivors.hint: Real Madrid won 2-1 at Hampden Park in Glasgow on 15 May 2002 to claim their ninth European title.

survivors.q: Which French player scored the spectacular left-footed volley that decided the 2002 Champions League final against Leverkusen?
survivors.hint: Zinedine Zidane volleyed in Roberto Carlos's looping cross on the stroke of half-time to make it 2-1 to Real Madrid.

survivors.q: Under which manager did Leverkusen win their first Bundesliga title in 2023-24?
survivors.hint: Xabi Alonso, appointed in October 2022, led Leverkusen to the 2023-24 Bundesliga crown in his first full season in charge.

survivors.q: Michael Ballack left Leverkusen in 2002 to join which club?
survivors.hint: Ballack moved to Bayern Munich in the summer of 2002 after three seasons at Leverkusen, and won the domestic double in his first year there.

survivors.q: Kai Havertz was sold by Leverkusen in 2020 to which club?
survivors.hint: Havertz joined Chelsea in September 2020 and scored the winning goal in that season's Champions League final.

survivors.q: Which South Korean player played for Leverkusen between 2013 and 2015 before moving to Tottenham Hotspur?
survivors.hint: Son Heung-min spent two seasons at the BayArena, arriving from Hamburger SV in 2013 and leaving for Tottenham in 2015.

survivors.q: What are Bayer Leverkusen's traditional club colours?
survivors.hint: Leverkusen have played in red and black for decades, with the Bayer cross carried on the badge.

survivors.q: Leverkusen won their first major European trophy in 1988. Which competition was it?
survivors.hint: Leverkusen lifted the UEFA Cup in 1988, still the club's only European trophy.

survivors.q: Which Spanish club did Leverkusen beat on penalties in the 1988 UEFA Cup final?
survivors.hint: Espanyol won the first leg 3-0 in Barcelona, but Leverkusen won the return 3-0 at the Ulrich-Haberland-Stadion and then took the shootout 3-2.

survivors.q: Who is Bayer Leverkusen's all-time leading Bundesliga goalscorer?
survivors.hint: Ulf Kirsten scored over 180 Bundesliga goals for Leverkusen between 1990 and 2003, and was the division's top scorer three times.

survivors.q: Ulf Kirsten joined Leverkusen in 1990 from which East German club?
survivors.hint: Kirsten made his name at Dynamo Dresden before crossing to Leverkusen shortly after German reunification.

survivors.q: Which club did Leverkusen beat in the 2024 DFB-Pokal final to complete the domestic double?
survivors.hint: Leverkusen beat second-division Kaiserslautern 1-0 in Berlin to win only their second DFB-Pokal.

survivors.q: Which Leverkusen player scored the only goal of the 2024 DFB-Pokal final?
survivors.hint: Granit Xhaka, signed from Arsenal in 2023, struck early in the final to settle the tie against Kaiserslautern.

survivors.q: Leverkusen's 2023-24 unbeaten run finally ended in the Europa League final against which Italian club?
survivors.hint: Atalanta won 3-0 in Dublin in May 2024, with Ademola Lookman scoring a hat-trick.

survivors.q: Which English club did Leverkusen eliminate in the semi-finals of the 2001-02 Champions League?
survivors.hint: Leverkusen drew 2-2 at Old Trafford and 1-1 at home, going through on away goals against Manchester United.

survivors.q: Which Brazilian defender scored Leverkusen's goal in the 2002 Champions League final?
survivors.hint: Lúcio headed in the first-half equaliser after Raúl had put Real Madrid ahead inside ten minutes.

survivors.q: Who managed Leverkusen during the 2001-02 season in which they finished runners-up in the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and Champions League?
survivors.hint: Klaus Toppmöller took charge in 2001 and oversaw the treble-of-second-places campaign that cemented the "Neverkusen" tag.

survivors.q: On the final day of the 1999-2000 Bundesliga season, Leverkusen lost 2-0 away to which club and handed Bayern Munich the title?
survivors.hint: A defeat at newly promoted SpVgg Unterhaching, including a Michael Ballack own goal, cost Leverkusen the title on goal difference.

survivors.q: Michael Ballack signed for Leverkusen in 1999 from which club?
survivors.hint: Ballack was part of Kaiserslautern's shock 1997-98 title-winning squad before his 1999 move to Leverkusen; Chemnitzer FC was the earlier club where he came through.

survivors.q: Which Bulgarian player played for Leverkusen from 2001 to 2006 before joining Tottenham Hotspur?
survivors.hint: Dimitar Berbatov arrived from CSKA Sofia in 2001 and spent five seasons at the BayArena before his move to England.

survivors.q: Which team did Xabi Alonso manage immediately before taking the Leverkusen job in 2022?
survivors.hint: Alonso coached Real Sociedad B in Spain's second and third tiers from 2019 until 2022.

survivors.q: Leverkusen clinched the 2023-24 Bundesliga title with a 5-0 home win, Florian Wirtz scoring a hat-trick, against which club?
survivors.hint: The 5-0 win over Werder Bremen on 14 April 2024 sealed the title with five matches still to play.

survivors.q: Which German coach led Leverkusen to the 1988 UEFA Cup?
survivors.hint: Erich Ribbeck was in charge for the 1988 triumph over Espanyol; he later managed the German national team.

survivors.q: Leverkusen won the 1993 DFB-Pokal final against the amateur/reserve side of which club?
survivors.hint: Hertha BSC's amateur team's run to the 1993 final remains unique in DFB-Pokal history; Leverkusen won it 1-0.

survivors.q: Leverkusen's captain missed the 2002 Champions League final after a cruciate ligament injury. Which Germany international was it?
survivors.hint: Jens Nowotny tore his cruciate in the semi-final second leg against Manchester United on 30 April 2002, and missed both the final and the World Cup that summer.

survivors.q: Which German goalkeeper started the 2002 Champions League final for Leverkusen?
survivors.hint: Hans-Jörg Butt, famous for taking penalties himself, was Leverkusen's first-choice keeper from 2001 to 2007.

survivors.q: How many matches long was the unbeaten run across all competitions that Leverkusen's 2023-24 side put together before losing to Atalanta?
survivors.hint: The 51-match unbeaten sequence set a record for a European top-flight club before it ended in the Europa League final.

survivors.q: Which manager did Xabi Alonso replace at Leverkusen in October 2022?
survivors.hint: Gerardo Seoane was dismissed after a poor start to 2022-23 with Leverkusen near the foot of the table.

survivors.q: Which German midfielder spent an 18-month loan spell at Leverkusen from Bayern Munich between 2009 and 2010?
survivors.hint: Toni Kroos joined Leverkusen on loan in January 2009 and stayed until June 2010, establishing himself as a first-team regular.

survivors.q: Which Chilean midfielder played for Leverkusen from 2007 to 2011 before joining Juventus?
survivors.hint: Arturo Vidal arrived from Colo-Colo as a teenager and spent four seasons at Leverkusen before his move to Turin.

survivors.q: What was the BayArena called before it was renamed in 1998?
survivors.hint: The ground was named the Ulrich-Haberland-Stadion after a former Bayer executive before adopting the BayArena name.

survivors.q: Which Brazilian midfielder left Leverkusen for Bayern Munich in 2002, in the same summer as Michael Ballack?
survivors.hint: Zé Roberto joined Leverkusen in 1998 and moved on to Bayern Munich in 2002 after the Champions League final defeat.

survivors.q: Which German midfielder, nicknamed "the white Brazilian" for his technique, played for Leverkusen from 1999 to 2009?
survivors.hint: Bernd Schneider spent a decade at Leverkusen and earned the nickname "der weiße Brasilianer" for his silky ball control.

survivors.q: How many points did Leverkusen finish the unbeaten 2023-24 Bundesliga season with?
survivors.hint: Leverkusen took 90 points from 34 games: 28 wins and six draws, with no defeats.

survivors.q: Olympique Lyonnais supporters know the club by which nickname?
survivors.hint: 'Gone' is Lyonnais dialect for a kid or lad, so Les Gones means 'the kids' — Les Verts are Saint-Étienne, Les Dogues are Lille and Les Aiglons are Nice.

survivors.q: Which stadium has been Lyon's home ground since 2016?
survivors.hint: Lyon moved into the purpose-built Parc Olympique Lyonnais in the east of the city in January 2016; the ground was renamed the Groupama Stadium when the naming-rights deal was signed in 2017.

survivors.q: Lyon dominated Ligue 1 in the 2000s with a French record run of consecutive league titles. How many did they win in a row?
survivors.hint: Lyon won seven straight French championships, a Ligue 1 record for consecutive titles, before the run finally ended.

survivors.q: Which striker came through Lyon's academy and was sold to Real Madrid in 2009?
survivors.hint: Karim Benzema graduated from Lyon's youth system, won Ligue 1 with the club and joined Real Madrid in the summer of 2009.

survivors.q: Lyon's fiercest derby rivalry is contested against which neighbouring club?
survivors.hint: Only about 60km separates the two cities, making Lyon v Saint-Étienne — the Derby Rhône-Alpes — one of French football's most hostile fixtures.

survivors.q: Which Lyon goalkeeper joined Tottenham Hotspur in 2012?
survivors.hint: Hugo Lloris captained Lyon before moving to Tottenham in August 2012, where he spent eleven years and was made club captain in 2015.

survivors.q: Which club has won the most UEFA Women's Champions League titles?
survivors.hint: Lyon's women's side has lifted the European trophy eight times, more than any other club in the competition's history.

survivors.q: Alexandre Lacazette left Lyon in 2017 to join which English club?
survivors.hint: Lacazette signed for Arsenal in July 2017 for a fee of around £46m, then a club-record signing for the Gunners.

survivors.q: Which Brazilian midfielder, a devastating free-kick specialist, captained Lyon through their title-winning years?
survivors.hint: Juninho Pernambucano spent eight seasons at Lyon from 2001, winning seven league titles and becoming famous for his dipping knuckleball free-kicks.

survivors.q: What colour are Lyon's traditional home shirts?
survivors.hint: Lyon's traditional home kit is a white shirt trimmed with the club's red and blue, the colours that also fill the OL crest.

survivors.q: Which manager led Lyon to the first Ligue 1 title in the club's history?
survivors.hint: Jacques Santini delivered Lyon's maiden French championship before leaving to take charge of the France national team.

survivors.q: Which manager was in charge for the last of Lyon's seven straight titles, a season that also brought the Coupe de France?
survivors.hint: Alain Perrin completed the domestic double in 2007-08, Lyon's seventh consecutive league crown and their last to date.

survivors.q: Lyon signed Juninho Pernambucano in 2001 from which Brazilian club?
survivors.hint: Juninho arrived from Vasco da Gama, where he had won the Copa Libertadores, and became Lyon's on-field leader for eight years.

survivors.q: Lyon completed a domestic double in 2008 by beating which club 1-0 in the Coupe de France final?
survivors.hint: Karim Benzema's goal beat Paris Saint-Germain at the Stade de France, adding the cup to Lyon's seventh straight league title.

survivors.q: Lyon knocked which Spanish club out of the Champions League in the 2009-10 last 16?
survivors.hint: Lyon beat Real Madrid 1-0 at home and drew 1-1 in the Bernabéu to go through 2-1 on aggregate, extending Madrid's run of last-16 exits.

survivors.q: Which club ended Lyon's run in the 2010 Champions League semi-finals?
survivors.hint: Bayern Munich won the first leg 1-0 in Munich through Arjen Robben, then thrashed Lyon 3-0 in the return with an Ivica Olić hat-trick to reach the 2010 final.

survivors.q: In the 2020 Champions League quarter-final in Lisbon, Lyon produced a huge upset by beating which English club 3-1?
survivors.hint: Lyon stunned Manchester City in the one-legged quarter-final, with Moussa Dembélé scoring twice off the bench to send Pep Guardiola's side out.

survivors.q: Which businessman took over as Lyon president in 1987 and oversaw the club's rise from the second division to seven league titles?
survivors.hint: Jean-Michel Aulas arrived in 1987 with his 'OL – Europe' project when Lyon were a second-division side, and ran the club for over three decades.

survivors.q: Which French defender left Lyon for Barcelona in 2007?
survivors.hint: Éric Abidal joined Barcelona from Lyon in 2007 and went on to win the Champions League twice in Catalonia.

survivors.q: Which French winger did Lyon sell to Chelsea in 2007?
survivors.hint: Florent Malouda moved to Chelsea in 2007 after four seasons at Lyon in which he won four league titles.

survivors.q: Which goalkeeper spent eleven years at Lyon, winning all seven consecutive titles, before joining Atlético Madrid in 2008?
survivors.hint: Grégory Coupet was Lyon's number one from 1997 to 2008, was named Ligue 1's best goalkeeper repeatedly, and left for Atlético Madrid.

survivors.q: Which Dutch forward did Lyon sign from Manchester United in January 2017?
survivors.hint: Memphis Depay's Lyon move revived his career after a difficult spell at Old Trafford, and he later left for Barcelona on a free transfer.

survivors.q: In which season did Lyon win the first Ligue 1 title in their history?
survivors.hint: Lyon were crowned French champions for the first time in 2001-02, launching their record run of seven in a row.

survivors.q: Roughly what is the capacity of Lyon's Groupama Stadium?
survivors.hint: The Parc Olympique Lyonnais holds just over 59,000, making it one of the largest club grounds in France.

survivors.q: Who is Olympique Lyonnais' all-time leading goalscorer?
survivors.hint: Fleury Di Nallo, nicknamed 'le Petit Prince de Gerland', scored 222 goals for Lyon across the 1960s and early 1970s.

survivors.q: Which of these France national team managers was Lyon's head coach from 1988 to 1993?
survivors.hint: Raymond Domenech managed Lyon for five years from 1988, long before he took charge of France and led them to the 2006 World Cup final.

survivors.q: Which Dutch club eliminated Lyon on penalties in the 2004-05 Champions League quarter-finals?
survivors.hint: PSV Eindhoven edged Lyon in a shootout after the tie finished level, then went out to Milan in the semi-finals on away goals.

survivors.q: Which midfielder did Tottenham sign from Lyon in 2019 for what was then a club-record fee?
survivors.hint: Tanguy Ndombele's move to Tottenham was worth around £54m, breaking Spurs' transfer record at the time.

survivors.q: Which French forward was Ligue 1's top scorer in 2014-15 with 27 goals?
survivors.hint: Alexandre Lacazette's 27 league goals for Lyon won him the golden boot and the French Player of the Year award, finishing ahead of Gignac's 21.

survivors.q: Lyon broke their transfer record in 2009 to sign Argentine striker Lisandro López from which club?
survivors.hint: Lisandro López arrived from Porto, where he had been the Portuguese league's top scorer, for a fee of around €24m.

survivors.q: Lyon clinched their first ever league title on the final day of the season by beating which club 3-1 at Gerland?
survivors.hint: Lens needed only a draw at Gerland to be champions, but Lyon won 3-1 to snatch the title on the last day of 2001-02.

survivors.q: Which manager led Lyon to the Champions League semi-finals in 2020?
survivors.hint: Rudi Garcia took over in October 2019 and guided Lyon past Juventus and Manchester City before a 3-0 semi-final defeat to Bayern Munich.

survivors.q: Lyon signed Brazilian striker Sonny Anderson in 1999 from which club?
survivors.hint: Anderson joined Lyon from Barcelona, having moved to Catalonia from Monaco two years earlier.

survivors.q: Which trophy did Lyon lift in 2001, beating Monaco 2-1 in the final?
survivors.hint: The 2001 Coupe de la Ligue, won 2-1 after extra time at the Stade de France, was Lyon's first major trophy since the 1973 Coupe de France and the launchpad for their era of dominance.

survivors.q: Lyon signed Ghanaian midfielder Michael Essien in 2003 from which French club?
survivors.hint: Essien joined from Bastia, won two titles at Lyon and was named Ligue 1 Player of the Year before Chelsea signed him in 2005.

survivors.q: Which club knocked Lyon out of the 2016-17 Europa League at the semi-final stage?
survivors.hint: Ajax won the first leg 4-1 in Amsterdam and survived a 3-1 defeat in Lyon to go through 5-4 on aggregate.

survivors.q: Parma play their home matches at which stadium?
survivors.hint: Parma have used the Stadio Ennio Tardini since 1923; the Dall'Ara is Bologna's home, the Ferraris belongs to Genoa and Sampdoria, and the Franchi to Fiorentina.

survivors.q: Parma are based in which Italian region?
survivors.hint: The city of Parma sits in Emilia-Romagna, the same region as Bologna and Sassuolo.

survivors.q: Which major trophy have Parma never won?
survivors.hint: Parma have won three Coppa Italias, two UEFA Cups and the 1993 Cup Winners' Cup, but their best league finish is second place in 1996-97.

survivors.q: Which competition did Parma win in 1993, beating Royal Antwerp in the final?
survivors.hint: Parma won the 1992-93 European Cup Winners' Cup, beating Royal Antwerp 3-1 in the final.

survivors.q: Which goalkeeper came through Parma's youth system before becoming Italy's World Cup-winning number one?
survivors.hint: Gianluigi Buffon was developed at Parma and broke into their first team as a teenager before winning the 2006 World Cup as Italy's first-choice keeper.

survivors.q: Which Argentine striker did Parma sign from River Plate in 1996?
survivors.hint: Hernán Crespo joined Parma from River Plate in 1996 and became the club's central striker for four seasons.

survivors.q: Which Colombia international played for Parma in the early 1990s?
survivors.hint: Faustino Asprilla signed for Parma in 1992 and was a key figure in the club's first European trophy-winning sides.

survivors.q: Parma's 1999 UEFA Cup final win came against which French club?
survivors.hint: Parma beat Marseille 3-0 in the 1999 UEFA Cup final to claim their second UEFA Cup.

survivors.q: After the club went bankrupt in 2015, the refounded Parma restarted in which division?
survivors.hint: The refounded club was admitted to Serie D, Italy's fourth tier, for the 2015-16 season.

survivors.q: Which defender spent seven seasons at Parma from 1995 before later captaining Italy to the 2006 World Cup?
survivors.hint: Fabio Cannavaro played for Parma from 1995 to 2002, winning the UEFA Cup there before his 2006 World Cup triumph as Italy's captain.

survivors.q: Which manager led Parma to their first Coppa Italia and their first two European trophies?
survivors.hint: Nevio Scala managed Parma from 1989 to 1996 and delivered the club's first major silverware, including the 1992 Coppa Italia, the 1993 Cup Winners' Cup and the 1995 UEFA Cup.

survivors.q: Parma's 1993 European final against Royal Antwerp was played at which stadium?
survivors.hint: The 1993 Cup Winners' Cup final between Parma and Royal Antwerp was played at Wembley in London.

survivors.q: Which Italian club did Parma beat in the 1995 UEFA Cup final?
survivors.hint: Parma beat Juventus 2-1 on aggregate in the all-Italian 1995 UEFA Cup final.

survivors.q: Which manager led Parma to the UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia double in 1999?
survivors.hint: Alberto Malesani took charge in 1998 and won both the UEFA Cup and the Coppa Italia in his first season.

survivors.q: Parma's best Serie A finish is second place. In which season did they achieve it?
survivors.hint: Parma finished runners-up to Juventus in 1996-97, the highest league placing in the club's history.

survivors.q: Which manager guided Parma to their record second-place Serie A finish?
survivors.hint: Carlo Ancelotti managed Parma from 1996 to 1998 and took them to second in Serie A in his first season, 1996-97.

survivors.q: Fabio Cannavaro joined Parma in 1995 from which club?
survivors.hint: Cannavaro came through Napoli's youth system and made his senior breakthrough there before moving to Parma in 1995.

survivors.q: Lilian Thuram joined Parma in 1996 from which club?
survivors.hint: Thuram began his career at Monaco and signed for Parma in 1996, staying five seasons.

survivors.q: Hernán Crespo left Parma in 2000 for which club, in what was then a world-record transfer fee?
survivors.hint: Crespo's 2000 move from Parma to Lazio set a new world transfer record at the time.

survivors.q: Gianfranco Zola left Parma in November 1996 to join which English club?
survivors.hint: Zola moved from Parma to Chelsea in November 1996 and was voted the Football Writers' Player of the Year that season.

survivors.q: Which company, whose 2003 collapse plunged the club into crisis, bankrolled Parma during their golden era?
survivors.hint: The dairy giant Parmalat, run by Calisto Tanzi, funded Parma from 1990 until its accounting scandal broke in 2003.

survivors.q: How many Coppa Italia titles have Parma won?
survivors.hint: Parma lifted the Coppa Italia in 1992, 1999 and 2002.

survivors.q: Against which club did Gianluigi Buffon make his Serie A debut for Parma in November 1995, aged 17?
survivors.hint: Buffon's first Serie A appearance was a goalless draw with AC Milan at the Tardini in November 1995.

survivors.q: Which club did Faustino Asprilla join when he left Parma in 1996?
survivors.hint: Asprilla moved from Parma to Kevin Keegan's Newcastle United in early 1996.

survivors.q: Parma beat which club in the 1993 European Super Cup, after Marseille were barred from taking part?
survivors.hint: European Cup holders Marseille were excluded following the French match-fixing scandal, so beaten finalists AC Milan faced Parma, who won 2-1 on aggregate.

survivors.q: Which Parma player scored in both legs of their 1995 UEFA Cup final win?
survivors.hint: Midfielder Dino Baggio scored in the first leg at the Tardini and again in the second leg to settle the tie against Juventus.

survivors.q: Which defender was among the scorers in Parma's 3-0 win over Marseille in the 1999 UEFA Cup final?
survivors.hint: Full-back Paolo Vanoli scored alongside Hernán Crespo and Enrico Chiesa in the 1999 final.

survivors.q: Which Parma forward scored the goal that ended AC Milan's long unbeaten run in Serie A in March 1993?
survivors.hint: Asprilla's finish gave Parma a 1-0 win in March 1993 and brought Milan's record-breaking unbeaten league sequence to an end.

survivors.q: Which manager took charge of Parma in the mid-1980s before joining AC Milan in 1987?
survivors.hint: Arrigo Sacchi's work at Parma, including knocking Milan out of the Coppa Italia, persuaded Silvio Berlusconi to hire him in 1987.

survivors.q: Which former Parma manager became president of the refounded club in 2015?
survivors.hint: Nevio Scala, who had managed Parma's 1990s trophy sides, took the presidency of the newly refounded club after the 2015 bankruptcy.

survivors.q: Which former Parma defender managed the refounded club to promotion out of Serie D in 2016?
survivors.hint: Luigi Apolloni, a defender in Parma's 1990s trophy sides, coached the refounded club to the Serie D title in 2015-16.

survivors.q: Which manager led Parma to consecutive promotions from Serie C to Serie A in 2017 and 2018?
survivors.hint: Roberto D'Aversa took over in 2016 and won promotion in back-to-back seasons, completing Parma's climb from Serie D to Serie A in three years.

survivors.q: Which defender captained Parma through all three promotions from Serie D back to Serie A?
survivors.hint: Alessandro Lucarelli stayed with the club after the 2015 bankruptcy and wore the armband for all three successive promotions.

survivors.q: Which Ballon d'Or winner spent the 1995-96 season at Parma between two spells at Barcelona?
survivors.hint: Hristo Stoichkov, the 1994 Ballon d'Or winner, left Barcelona for Parma in 1995 and returned to the Camp Nou a year later.

survivors.q: Parma lost the 1994 Cup Winners' Cup final to which club?
survivors.hint: Arsenal beat holders Parma 1-0 in Copenhagen in the 1994 Cup Winners' Cup final through Alan Smith's volley.

survivors.q: Which Japan international joined Parma in 2001 and was part of the squad that won the 2002 Coppa Italia?
survivors.hint: Hidetoshi Nakata moved from Roma to Parma in 2001 and won the Coppa Italia with the club the following season.

name: AS Monaco

survivors.q: In which country's top division does AS Monaco play its league football?
survivors.hint: Although the club is based in the Principality of Monaco, it has competed in the French league system throughout its history.

survivors.q: What is the name of AS Monaco's home stadium?
survivors.hint: Monaco have played at the Stade Louis II, built on land reclaimed from the sea, since it opened in January 1985.

survivors.q: Which manager led Monaco to the 2016-17 Ligue 1 title?
survivors.hint: Portuguese coach Leonardo Jardim took charge in 2014 and guided Monaco to the championship in 2016-17.

survivors.q: Which club beat Monaco in the 2004 Champions League final?
survivors.hint: José Mourinho's Porto won the 2004 final 3-0 at the Arena AufSchalke in Gelsenkirchen.

survivors.q: Which club did Kylian Mbappé move to from Monaco in 2017?
survivors.hint: Mbappé joined Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2017, immediately after Monaco's title-winning season.

survivors.q: Monaco's traditional home shirt is famously split diagonally into which two colours?
survivors.hint: The diagonal red-and-white shirt has been Monaco's signature look for decades.

survivors.q: Which manager was in charge of Monaco from 1987 to 1994 before later taking over at Arsenal?
survivors.hint: Arsène Wenger won the French title in his first season at Monaco in 1987-88 and stayed until 1994.

survivors.q: How many times have Monaco won the French top division?
survivors.hint: Monaco's eight championships came in 1961, 1963, 1978, 1982, 1988, 1997, 2000 and 2017.

survivors.q: Which Colombian striker joined Monaco from Atlético Madrid in 2013?
survivors.hint: Radamel Falcao was the marquee signing of Monaco's spending spree after promotion back to Ligue 1.

survivors.q: Which club finished runners-up to Monaco in Ligue 1 in 2016-17?
survivors.hint: Monaco finished eight points clear of defending champions Paris Saint-Germain in 2016-17.

survivors.q: Which club did Monaco eliminate on away goals in the 2003-04 Champions League quarter-finals?
survivors.hint: Monaco lost 4-2 in Madrid but won the return leg 3-1 to go through 5-5 on away goals.

survivors.q: Which Spanish forward, on loan at Monaco from Real Madrid, was top scorer of the 2003-04 Champions League with nine goals?
survivors.hint: Fernando Morientes, on loan from parent club Real Madrid, was the outright top scorer of the 2003-04 Champions League with nine goals.

survivors.q: Who was Monaco's manager for the 2004 Champions League final?
survivors.hint: Didier Deschamps coached Monaco from 2001 to 2005 and took them to the 2004 final.

survivors.q: Which manager led Monaco to the 1996-97 French league title?
survivors.hint: Jean Tigana's 1996-97 champions included Fabien Barthez, Thierry Henry, David Trezeguet and Emmanuel Petit.

survivors.q: Which goalkeeper spent his entire career at Monaco, making 755 appearances between 1975 and 1994?
survivors.hint: Jean-Luc Ettori's 602 league games stood as the French top-flight appearance record until Mickaël Landreau passed it in 2013.

survivors.q: Which German club did Monaco knock out in the 2016-17 Champions League quarter-finals?
survivors.hint: Monaco won 3-2 away and 3-1 at home to eliminate Borussia Dortmund 6-3 on aggregate.

survivors.q: Monaco eliminated which English club on away goals in the 2016-17 Champions League round of 16?
survivors.hint: After losing 5-3 at the Etihad, Monaco won the return 3-1 to go through 6-6 on away goals against Manchester City.

survivors.q: Monaco's only Coupe de la Ligue triumph came in which year?
survivors.hint: Monaco beat Sochaux 4-1 in the 2003 final at the Stade de France for their sole French League Cup.

survivors.q: Which African player began his European career at Monaco in 1988 after signing from Tonnerre Yaoundé?
survivors.hint: George Weah arrived from Cameroonian club Tonnerre Yaoundé in 1988 and won the Coupe de France with Monaco in 1991.

survivors.q: At the end of which season were Monaco relegated to Ligue 2?
survivors.hint: Monaco went down in 2011, their first relegation from the French top flight in 35 years.

survivors.q: Which businessman bought a two-thirds stake in AS Monaco in December 2011?
survivors.hint: Dmitry Rybolovlev acquired 66.67% of the club in December 2011, when Monaco were bottom of Ligue 2.

survivors.q: Which manager guided Monaco to the Ligue 2 title in 2012-13 and promotion back to the top flight?
survivors.hint: Claudio Ranieri took over from Marco Simone and won the second division at the first attempt in 2012-13.

survivors.q: From which Argentine club did Monaco sign David Trezeguet in 1995?
survivors.hint: Trezeguet moved from Platense to Monaco in 1995 and went on to win two French titles there before joining Juventus.

survivors.q: Which club beat Monaco 2-0 in the 1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final?
survivors.hint: Otto Rehhagel's Werder Bremen won the Lisbon final through goals from Klaus Allofs and Wynton Rufer.

survivors.q: In which year was AS Monaco founded?
survivors.hint: The club was founded on 23 August 1924.

survivors.q: How many goals did Monaco score in Ligue 1 during their 2016-17 title season?
survivors.hint: Monaco scored a league-high 107 goals and finished the campaign on 95 points.

survivors.q: Which club did Monaco beat 4-2 in the 1960 Coupe de France final to win the first major trophy in their history?
survivors.hint: Monaco beat Saint-Étienne 4-2 at Colombes in May 1960 for their first major honour.

survivors.q: Who was Monaco's manager when they won the 1977-78 French title in the season straight after promotion?
survivors.hint: Lucien Leduc's side came up and immediately took the 1977-78 championship, finishing a point clear of Nantes.

survivors.q: Which club knocked Monaco out of the 1997-98 Champions League at the semi-final stage?
survivors.hint: Juventus won the first leg 4-1 in Turin, with Alessandro Del Piero scoring a hat-trick, and advanced 6-4 on aggregate.

survivors.q: Whose record as Monaco's youngest first-team player did Kylian Mbappé break in December 2015?
survivors.hint: Mbappé was 16 years and 347 days old on his debut against Caen, beating Thierry Henry's mark of 17 years and 14 days.

survivors.q: Which Mexican defender played for Monaco from 1999 to 2003 before joining Barcelona?
survivors.hint: Rafael Márquez won the 1999-2000 French title in his first season at Monaco and moved to Barcelona in 2003.

survivors.q: In which season did Monaco win the French league championship and the Coupe de France in the same campaign?
survivors.hint: Monaco completed the domestic double in 1962-63, adding the Coupe de France to their second league title.

survivors.q: Which German striker did Monaco sign from Internazionale in 1992?
survivors.hint: Arsène Wenger brought Jürgen Klinsmann to Monaco after he left Inter in 1992; he stayed two seasons before joining Tottenham Hotspur in 1994.

skepticReasons: Answer and stem are right (Pršo scored four on 5 Nov 2003, his 29th birthday — confirmed by UEFA and contemporary CNN report), but the hint's superlative is now false: 'set Champions League records for goals by one side' no longer holds — Dortmund 8-4 Legia Warsaw (Nov 2016) took the aggregate record and Liverpool 8-0 Beşiktaş equalled eight by one side. Rewriting the hint without the stale superlative.

FALSE PREMISE in the stem. Delio Onnis was born in Giuliano di Roma, ITALY, on 24 March 1948 and emigrated to Argentina as a child (nicknamed 'El Tano'). Every distractor (Bianchi, Díaz, Combin) IS genuinely Argentina-born, so as written the qualifier excludes the keyed answer and admits only wrong options — deletion-grade. The underlying fact is sound (157 league goals for Monaco, 1973-1980), so the fix is to say 'Argentine' rather than 'Argentina-born'.

Answer o[2]='299' is right and both stem claims hold (Onnis is Monaco's record scorer and the French top-flight all-time record holder), but the hint's date range is contested — sources give his Division 1 scoring span as 1972-1986 rather than 1971-1986, and the precise start year adds nothing. Dropping the disputed years rather than shipping a number I can't settle.
